summary: Iteration 4 testing - Orders date filter (from/to + Today/7d/30d/This month/Clear), CSV export with token query param + filename 'sales_*', and Customers FIFO payment (record_customer_payment + dialog + drawer button). Backend: 55/55 pytest passing (39 prior + 16 new across TestOrdersDateFilter, TestOrdersCsvExport, TestCustomerPayment). Frontend: live e2e on https://plumb-stock-pro.preview.emergentagent.com confirms all flows: Today/This month presets fire /api/orders?from_date=&to_date=, Clear resets, Export triggers CSV download (sales_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv), customer Pay button opens dialog pre-filled to outstanding, partial payment closes dialog, success toast appears, row badge updates immediately (50735.38 -> 50725.38 after Rs10 payment), drawer Record-payment opens same dialog.
critical_code_review_comments: POST /api/customers/{cid}/payment is not idempotent and does not run inside a transaction - if the orders.update_one calls succeed but customers.update_one fails (or vice-versa), customer.current_balance and order due_amount will diverge. Wrap allocation + balance decrement in a single MongoDB session/transaction or persist a payments collection as the source of truth.

record_customer_payment has no role gating - any authenticated user (incl. staff) can record payments and decrement balances. Likely should be admin-only or at minimum logged with stronger audit (already logs, but no rate-limit or duplicate-detection).

GET /api/orders/export.csv accepts ?token= query param which is convenient but tokens leak into server access logs/browser history/referrer headers. Mitigation: short-lived signed download tokens or POST + 302 + temp signed URL. At minimum, document the trade-off.
Export streams entire result set into memory via to_list(100000) before writing CSV. For large stores this will OOM the worker. Consider StreamingResponse with an async generator that yields rows.

list_orders date filter compares created_at (string ISO) with string range. Works because ISO-8601 sorts lexicographically, but the to_date upper bound 'YYYY-MM-DDT23:59:59.999999' is naive (no TZ suffix) and orders stored as UTC ISO without 'Z' could behave unexpectedly across timezones. Use proper datetime objects.
The CSV BOM (\ufeff) is correctly prepended for Excel compatibility but is undocumented. Confirm front-end download path handles BOM (it does, because browser saves bytes verbatim).
server.py is now ~1670 lines (carry-over). Splitting into routers becoming overdue.
Carry-over from iter 3: order cancel + status PATCH still ungated; tasks PATCH ungated; audit_logs no TTL.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on tested flows (date presets, clear, export download, customer pay dialog + drawer pay + row update)
